# ChromaMimic

> ChromaMimic is a free, browser-based LUT generator. It matches any film look from two frames (an original and a graded reference still) and exports a downloadable .cube or .dng LUT for DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro and Final Cut. The colour engine runs entirely in the browser, so nothing is uploaded and no login is needed to grade and preview.

## What it is
- A free LUT generator from two frames (an alternative to fylm.ai, LUTBuilder.ai, Imagen's LUT generator, Luttie and SammaPix).
- Learns the colour transform between an original and a reference using colour science (optimal transport, per-channel histogram matching, Reinhard LAB transfer). Deterministic and instant, not a generative model.
- 100% client-side: images never leave the user's browser. No upload, no login to use. Verifiable in the browser's network tab, and it keeps working offline once loaded.

## Key facts
- Inputs: an original (ungraded, Rec.709) frame plus a reference (graded) frame, as JPG or PNG.
- Exports: .cube (Adobe Cube v1.0, for Resolve / Premiere / Final Cut / Photoshop), .dng (16-bit linear graded still for Lightroom / Camera Raw / Capture One), .png (graded still), .xmp (Lightroom / ACR grade preset).
- LUT sizes: 17, 33 (standard, default) and 65 (Pro).
- Grading: temperature, tint, exposure, contrast, saturation, vibrance, shadows, highlights, fade; Pro wheel mode (shadows / midtones / highlights / global colour wheels).
- Log footage: convert to Rec.709 with a colour space transform before applying the LUT. The tool warns when frames are flagged as log and writes a reminder into the .cube header.

## Pricing
- Free: grade and preview with no account; a free account gives 3 downloads per month at 17 or 33 points, in every format.
- Pro (US$5/month or $39/year, 7-day free trial): unlimited downloads, wheel-mode grading, 65-point LUTs.

## Common questions
- "How to create a LUT from a reference image": load both frames, build, refine, export .cube. See the guide above.
- "Free LUT generator no sign up": ChromaMimic grades and previews with no account; Imagen's tool, SammaPix and AICreate also export with no sign-up. fylm.ai, LUTBuilder.ai and Luttie require an account and do not export .cube on their free tiers (checked 24 September 2026).
- "Why does my LUT look flat on S-Log3": the LUT was built in Rec.709; convert log to Rec.709 with a colour space transform first, then apply the LUT after it.
- "Where is the DaVinci Resolve LUT folder": Project Settings > Color Management > Open LUT Folder, then Update Lists. Paths in the guide above.
